title: fix(plugin-kanban): hang the board's empty state on settled, not on zero rows (objectui#8827)
body:
Part of #8827

⚠️ **`Part of`, not `Fixes`, deliberately.** This PR closes ruling ①–④ of the PM
re-ruling (comment 5602422263) — the lying predicate. Two items the same ruling
kept **open on the card** would be silently dropped if merging closed it:
ruling ⑤ leaves **option A (ordering the chunk against the data)** unruled and
on the card, and the card's **question 3 (other `React.lazy` surfaces)** stays
**NOT MEASURED**. Close #8827 by hand once those are dispositioned.

## The defect

`KanbanImpl` paints `DataEmptyState` — a `role="status" aria-live="polite"` live
region titled **No cards** — whenever the board holds zero cards across more
than one lane (`KanbanImpl.tsx:865`, `:868-874`). That predicate is an assertion
*about the data*, and the component was making it **before it had the data**.

`KanbanRenderer` loads `KanbanImpl` behind `React.lazy`, so the chunk's arrival
and the records' arrival are two unordered events (objectui#8534's second half;
the mirror half was closed by PR #8825 and is **not** this). On the production
shape — lanes derived synchronously from `schema.columns`, rows arriving from
`ObjectKanban`'s query — the previous round measured both orderings on
post-#8825 `main` and they diverge: when the data wins, the Suspense skeleton
covers the whole window; **when the chunk wins, the first committed frame
announces a false "No cards" to assistive technology while the rows are still in
flight.** The only thing hiding it was the lazy skeleton happening to be slower
than the fetch.

## What changed

The empty-state predicate now hangs on **settled**, not on "zero rows".

- **A keyed resolution, not a boolean.** `ObjectKanban`'s existing `loading`
  state cannot express this and wiring it in would have fixed nothing: in
  standalone mode it initialises `false` (`ObjectKanban.tsx:280`) and is only set
  `true` inside the fetch *effect* (`:341`), so the first frame still reads
  `loading === false`. A bare boolean takes the same value for "not started" and
  "finished". The shape here is `useSettledSchema`'s (objectui#6271 / #7225,
  maintainer ruling B): one piece of state carrying the key it settled for, with
  "settled" derived at render, so "settled for the wrong object" — objectui#6481's
  one-way-latch defect — is unrepresentable rather than merely fixed.
- **A package-private channel.** `ObjectKanban` provides, `KanbanImpl` consumes;
  context crosses the `Suspense`/`lazy` boundary normally. See the Clause-②
  section below for the verified reason this is not a published surface.
- **The per-lane placeholder takes the same gate.** `KanbanColumnView` renders
  the same `kanban.noCards` string, and on a **single-lane** board the
  board-level predicate never runs (it requires `boardColumns.length > 1`) — so
  gating only the live region would have left the false claim alive on exactly
  the boards the live region never covered.

## What did NOT change

Ruling ④'s reverse regression is named in this very file — *"gating on a truthy
definition would leave those boards empty forever"* (`ObjectKanban.tsx:276`).
Every exit settles:

| Exit | How it settles |
|---|---|
| 1. query succeeds | `settleRecords()` in the fetch `finally` |
| 2. query throws | same `finally` — one place, so neither can be added to without the other |
| 3. no readable source (no `dataSource` / no `find` / no `objectName`) | **structurally**, by `recordsComeFromFetch` at render, plus a redundant settle at `fetchData`'s own guard |
| 4. non-fetch sources (external / bound / inline `schema.data`) | **structurally** — settled from the first frame |
| 5. schema-only `kanban-ui` entry (no `ObjectKanban` ⇒ **no provider**) | the context **default is `true`** |

Lanes, headers, counts and drop targets keep rendering while rows are in flight;
only the *claim* is withheld. No chunk boundary moved, no first paint was
delayed, `React.lazy` is untouched, and `KanbanImpl`'s mirror sync (#8534 /
PR #8825 / objectui#4138) was not touched.

## Acceptance — both legs, and the ablations that prove they can fail

`pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-kanban/src/__tests__/recordsSettledEmptyState-8827.test.tsx`
→ **7 passed, exit 0**. Full package suite `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban test`
→ **42 files, 260 tests passed, exit 0**.

The rig carries its own self-checks, because the previous round's first run had
too small a flush budget and every ordering sat on the Suspense fallback looking
identical — an instrument that had never connected reading as "no difference".
The forward test asserts the chunk **is** held (`expect(boardIsMounted()).toBe(false)`),
asserts it **landed** after release, and asserts the end state it converges to.
A run that fails to reproduce the race goes **red**; it can never read as a pass.

⚠️ **Leg 1 alone proves nothing — deleting the empty state would also make it
green.** So each ablation below states its predicted direction first, and the
observed direction is reported as observed:

| Ablation | Predicted | **Observed** |
|---|---|---|
| **A** — `showEmptyState = isBoardEmpty` (drop the gate) | forward RED, reverse GREEN | ✅ as predicted — `× paints no empty state while the records are still in flight`, 1 failed / 6 passed |
| **B** — context default `false` | reverse **exit 5** RED, forward GREEN | ✅ as predicted — `× exit 5 — the schema-only kanban-ui entry has NO provider and DEFAULTS to settled`, 1 failed / 6 passed |
| **C** — neuter the effect-side settle only | reverse **exit 1** RED (1 test) | ⚠️ **2 tests red, not 1.** exit 1 **plus** the single-lane test, whose *second* half (`then paints it`) is a second instance of the same "empty forever" guard. Exits 3/4/5 stayed **green**, which was the sharp half of the prediction and held: the structural settle really is independent of the effect settle. |

Every ablation was proved on disk before its run (anchor count → 0, injected
count → 1) and proved restored after (`git diff HEAD` empty, worktree blob hash
back to the HEAD blob). ⚠️ Ablation C's **first** attempt refused itself: the
multi-line anchor made `grep -c` count lines rather than occurrences, the on-disk
proof read it as a no-op and voided the run. It was re-run with a countable
single-line anchor rather than silently retried until something landed.

## Clause-②: no — premises verified against the tree, not taken on trust

The re-ruling asked for three premises to be checked rather than trusted:

1. **`package.json` has a single `.` entry** — ⚠️ *precise reading*: `exports`
   has **two** keys, `.` and `./style.css`. Only one is a module entry; the
   second maps to `dist/index.css`, a stylesheet, which cannot re-export a
   module. Premise holds in substance. There is **no `./*` subpath**.
2. **`index.tsx` carries no `export *`** — confirmed, 0 occurrences.
3. **`KanbanImpl` is not in the export list** — confirmed; it appears only as
   `React.lazy(() => import('./KanbanImpl'))` and in doc comments.

⇒ A module-level context not re-exported from `index.tsx` adds nothing to the
published surface. **Measured on the built artifact**, with a lit control:
`dist/index.d.ts` contains **0** mentions of `KanbanRecordsSettled` /
`useKanbanRecordsSettled`, while the control symbol `KanbanRendererProps` hits
**3** times — so the instrument is connected and the zero is a reading.

⚠️ One thing stated rather than glossed: `vite-plugin-dts` emits a per-file
`dist/KanbanRecordsSettled.d.ts` into the tarball, exactly as it already emits
`dist/KanbanImpl.d.ts`. Neither is reachable through the export map. This adds
no new *kind* of artifact and no new reachable surface — `KanbanImpl` has been
in that exact position all along.

⛔ This was not a contortion to dodge the gate. Routing the signal as a member of
`KanbanRendererProps` would put a new key on a **published** payload for a value
no external caller may set; routing it through the `schema` bag would be worse
still, since `BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()` and an author could write it on the
`kanban-ui` entry — the exact shape objectui#7742 / decision batch #70 moved
`objectFields` off. The context is a strictly **narrower** channel, not the same
channel hidden.

## Verification run locally

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban lint` (the package's full `eslint .`) | exit 0 — 180 pre-existing warnings, **0** attributable to the new/edited files |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban test` | 42 files / 260 tests, exit 0 |
| `check:control-bytes` · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` · `check:unreferenced-sources` · `check:side-effects-array` · `check:i18n-keys` · `check:self-import` | all exit 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence` · `check-changeset-no-major` | exit 0 |
| Governed Surface Queue Guard | **NOT GOVERNED** (exit 0), with `AGENTS.md` as the lit control returning **GOVERNED** (exit 3) — the instrument is connected |

⚠️ **Declared narrowing — `check:eager-closure` is NOT MEASURED locally.** It
weighs `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`, which only a console build emits,
and that build fails here on its own unbuilt dependency closure
(`@object-ui/plugin-form`, `@object-ui/auth`) — a broken gauge, not a failed
budget. Building it is a whole-repo build and belongs to CI. In its place, the
bundle question was measured directly, trap-guarded: `plugin-kanban`'s
`dist/index.js` goes **57858 → 58403 bytes (+545)**, and reverting the three
files rebuilt to exactly 57858 and restoring rebuilt to exactly 58403 — a clean
round trip on both legs.

All readings above are from the final commit `9afd15ba0`.
